key_insight: Measured, open retention data on U.S. PDKs lowers entry cost for gain-cell IP and trains a domestic memory workforce; a useful by-product of any MPW dossier.
killer_doubt: A 130 nm 3T or MIM 1T1C cell is ~1-3 um2/bit, ~500-1,000x a 1b cell (0.0023 um2), with ~ms retention at 85 C. 22FDX is not an open PDK.
decisive_experiment: One Sky130/GF180 shuttle (~$20-50k): 64 kb 3T and MIM 1T1C macros with retention BIST; compare bits/mm2 and 85 C retention against OpenGCRAM and RAAAM published figures.
prior_art: OpenRAM (UCSC), OpenGCRAM open gain-cell compiler, RAAAM GCRAM IP; review I-11121 already dropped the same open-PDK test-chip idea.

key_insight: A fully depleted, surface-pinned node removes interface generation, the main Si leakage path; charge moves through a semiconductor channel, so write endurance is unlimited.
killer_doubt: Dark current doubles every ~6-8 C: 5 e-/s at 25 C becomes ~1,000-3,000 e-/s at 85 C, so 2,000 e- lasts ~0.1-0.5 s. Cells ~0.5 um2, ~200x 1b.
decisive_experiment: Reuse an existing global-shutter CIS test chip, no tapeout: write the storage diode by fill-and-spill, histogram 85 C dark current over 1e6 nodes, and time the transfer. ~$50k.
prior_art: Global-shutter CIS in-pixel pinned storage diodes (Sony, onsemi); 1970s CCD memories; IGZO 2T0C already gives >400 s retention at far smaller area.

key_insight: Areal capacitance, not aspect ratio, is the real lever: a 30x30 nm pad at ~500 uF/cm2 would hold ~4.5 fF and delete the 60:1 etch.
killer_doubt: Proton diffusion (D ~1e-8 to 1e-10 cm2/s) across 5 nm takes ~25 us-2.5 ms, 1e3-1e5x too slow; Faradaic films survive ~1e5-1e6 cycles versus >=3e8 needed.
decisive_experiment: Probe-station RuO2 or MXene micro-pads on a thin proton conductor (~$100k): capacitance versus frequency from 1 kHz to 100 MHz, then capacitance retained after 1e8 pulses at 0.5 V.
prior_art: Hydrous RuO2 and MXene micro-supercapacitors; MIT nanosecond protonic programmable resistors (Science 2022) move far fewer ions per pulse at high field (training knowledge).

key_insight: Donor-wafer reuse decouples crystal cost from tier count, and pre-tested single-crystal membranes avoid the Si/SiGe superlattice defects of monolithic 3D DRAM.
killer_doubt: Si remote epitaxy fails through graphene (covalent field is screened). Floating-body cells hold only tens of ms at 85 C; 64 bonds at 99.5% each give 73% stacks.
decisive_experiment: CVD Si on graphene-coated Si(001), check registry by EBSD/XRD (~$80k); in parallel, measure 85 C retention tails on existing SOI floating-body test chips. Either failure kills it.
prior_art: Kong et al., Nat. Mater. 2018: Si/Ge remote epitaxy fails through graphene (via search snippet); Soitec Smart Cut and Canon ELTRAN donor reuse; Z-RAM.

key_insight: Compiler-known lifetimes can drop refresh for genuinely short-lived buffers, and a hardware TTL fault makes the expiry contract checkable.
killer_doubt: KV caches live seconds to minutes, training activations ~0.1-10 s per step; rewriting before expiry is refresh. A 3x smaller Cs needs ~3x lower leakage to keep 100 ms.
decisive_experiment: Instrument vLLM serving and one training run to histogram DRAM page lifetimes; kill if <20% of bytes die within 50 ms. Then disable refresh on an FPGA DDR4 rig. ~$30k.
prior_art: RANA (ISCA 2018) retention-aware eDRAM for DNNs; Flikker; RAIDR; Phase B N-64 lifetime-leased refresh; review I-04810 dropped the same idea.

key_insight: MR4 refresh-rate reporting lets stock DDR5 controllers run a weak-retention die at 2x or 4x refresh with no host changes.
killer_doubt: Post-repair, post-on-die-ECC retention fallout is ~1-3% of dies; at 32 Gb 4x refresh costs ~42% bandwidth (tRFC 410 ns, tREFI 0.98 us). Downgrade bins already sell.
decisive_experiment: Partner with a module house holding downgrade dies: retention-map 1,000 fallout parts at 32 ms and 16 ms windows, 85 C; report the share passing at 2x refresh.
prior_art: Micron SpecTek and other downgrade channels; DDR5 2x refresh above 85 C; review I-07481 (temperature-grade resale) dropped.

key_insight: Area cost, not density, sets $/bit: an IGZO 1T1C at ~0.02 um2 (0.7 fF planar) gives ~3-6 TB/m2, so even $300/m2 lands near $0.05-0.1/GB.
killer_doubt: At 50 nm, ~6 aligned layers need ~10-15 nm overlay; polyimide moves 10-20 ppm/K, 100-200 nm per kelvin across 1 cm. Spatial-ALD IGZO Vt sigma at 50 nm is unknown.
decisive_experiment: Fold into the I-01819 demo: one multilevel SAIL stamp at 50 and 100 nm on steel foil on carrier; measure overlay, killer defects/cm2 and 85 C 1T1C retention. ~$400k.
prior_art: HP Labs SAIL roll-to-roll TFTs; PragmatIC IGZO FlexICs; this study's I-01819 (advanced by two critics) is the same mechanism at 100 nm.

key_insight: Strain-driven self-rolling compacts a planar array ~40-60x in footprint with one release etch, which could pack bits under an accelerator.
killer_doubt: Rolling creates no bits: 20 windings need 20x footprint of patterned area, so $/bit equals planar DUV TFT cost (~20-50x 1b). R=5 um bends a 100 nm stack 1%.
decisive_experiment: Roll a released SiNx bilayer carrying a 32x32 IGZO TFT array (~$150k university fab); measure Vt shift, yield per winding and edge-contact yield at the tube end.
prior_art: Rolled-up nanomembranes (Prinz; Schmidt group, IFW Dresden): rolled capacitors, microbatteries, sensors (training knowledge); rolled memory arrays: none found.

key_insight: Crosspoint decks remove the lateral access transistor, the main 3D DRAM blocker, and idle chalcogenide PVD tooling exists.
killer_doubt: OTS sub-threshold leakage is ~1e-11 to 1e-9 A at ~0.5 V; on 5 fF at 0.5 V, tau = CV/I ~2.5 us-0.25 ms. Needs ~8 fA: a 1e3-1e5x miracle.
decisive_experiment: Build 1S1C test cells (OTS in series with a 5 fF MIM, ~$100k); measure node decay at 25 and 85 C under V/2 biasing; kill if retention is under 1 ms.
prior_art: Intel/Micron 3D XPoint OTS selectors; Phase B N-85 and N-87 1S1C selector-DRAM; review I-08787 dropped an OTS 1S1C cell.

key_insight: Each access transistor acts as a current source, so plating is self-aligned and dead cells grow nothing: a built-in electrical yield screen.
killer_doubt: Mold-free plating grows isotropically: from 20 nm seeds at ~40 nm pitch, neighbours merge at ~20 nm height, ~60x short of a 1.2 um node. Free AR-100 pillars collapse anyway.
decisive_experiment: Seed-array test wafer (e-beam 20 nm pads, 40 nm pitch, ~$60k): plate Ni or Ru with and without suppressor additives; measure height at first merge by SEM.
prior_art: Template electrodeposition (AAO and track-etch nanowires); SiN-supported DRAM pillar capacitors; transistor-gated self-plating of storage nodes: none found.

key_insight: A matched-lifetime tier is the logical end of refresh-free design; at ~100 us a planar 0.5 fF node needs only ~1 pA leakage, trivially met.
killer_doubt: Little's law: capacity <= bandwidth x lifetime. At HBM3E's ~1.2 TB/s per stack, 100 us holds ~120 MB, SRAM-scale and already on-die (H100 has 50 MB L2).
decisive_experiment: Trace an LLM inference and a training step on GPU; count bytes whose write-to-last-read interval is under 100 us yet spill off-chip; kill if <5% of DRAM traffic. ~$20k.
prior_art: RANA (ISCA 2018), gain-cell eDRAM for DNN accelerators, refresh-free eDRAM buffers; review I-04810 dropped the same class.

key_insight: At 0.01-0.02 fF one electron is ~8-16 mV, so 50 e- give ~0.4-0.8 V: read noise vanishes and skipper averaging is unnecessary. The real question is minimum charge per bit.
killer_doubt: Holding 50 e- within 10 e- for 1 s needs <=1.6 aA at the 1e-6 tail; one Si midgap trap emits ~1e3 e-/s at 85 C; skipper samples ~10 us.
decisive_experiment: IGZO 2T0C array with a minimal ~0.02 fF node on a university BEOL line (~$300k): map per-cell charge loss in electrons over 1e4 cells at 85 C, plus 1e6 neighbour-wordline toggles.
prior_art: Skipper CCDs (Tiffenberg et al., PRL 2017) reach 0.068 e- rms over ms (training knowledge); imec IGZO 2T0C and IGZO CCD memory store sub-1,000 e-.
